title: Harden Review-to-Implementation Feedback Contract And Block No-Op Followups
specification:
# PRD: Harden Review-to-Implementation Feedback Contract And Block No-Op Followups

Priority: high

## Problem
Reviewer feedback is preserved as conversation continuity and prose summaries, but it is not converted into machine-enforced follow-up requirements. Implementation follow-ups can complete as `noop` with no new evidence, and reviewer auto-approval can merge PRs after repeated rounds even when the original blocker was not substantively satisfied.

## Goal
Make reviewer feedback actionable and enforceable so implementation follow-ups must either produce the requested proof or remain blocked, while preserving conversation continuity for both implementation and review agents.

## Requirements
- Convert review change requests into structured follow-up requirements, including explicit required checks, expected evidence, and blocker categories.
- Persist those structured requirements onto implementation follow-up tasks instead of only copying summary prose into description/acceptance.
- Prevent implementation follow-up completion as `noop` when unresolved structured review blockers remain open.
- Allow reviewer to approve only when structured blockers are satisfied or explicitly dismissed by policy.
- Scope auto-approval so it cannot override unresolved verification blockers.
- Preserve and display implementation and review conversation references, but treat them as continuity aids rather than proof of requirement satisfaction.
- Surface in queue/state data whether a follow-up closed each reviewer blocker and what evidence was recorded.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A review requesting a focused test run creates a follow-up task that records that test command as a required check or required evidence item.
- An implementation follow-up with no code changes and no new required evidence cannot transition to done/merged while blockers remain open.
- Reviewer approval is blocked when unresolved structured blockers exist, even after repeated rounds.
- A PR history view shows which reviewer blockers were opened, which follow-up addressed them, and whether they were satisfied.
- Existing conversation resume behavior for implementation and review remains intact.

## Verification
- Unit tests for follow-up task creation proving review feedback becomes structured requirements.
- Unit tests for implementation completion logic proving unresolved blockers prevent `noop` completion.
- Unit tests for reviewer decision logic proving auto-approval does not bypass unresolved verification blockers.
- Smoke test covering a review-requested focused verification flow from review -> follow-up -> approval.

tasks.title: Persist structured reviewer blockers onto implementation follow-up tasks
tasks.description: Implement the review-to-follow-up contract so reviewer change requests are normalized into structured blocker records and copied onto implementation follow-up tasks as machine-readable requirements rather than prose-only summaries. Preserve existing implementation/review conversation references for continuity, but store explicit blocker categories, required checks, expected evidence, and per-blocker status in queue/state data that later steps can enforce. Likely touch points include review follow-up creation and queue/spec persistence under `src/autonomy-v2/commands/`, `src/sync/`, and tracked prompt/spec helpers under `prompts/autonomous/v2/` templates or runtime serializers if they participate in task creation.
acceptance: A review change request that asks for a focused verification step creates an implementation follow-up task containing a structured blocker or requirement entry with the requested test command captured as a required check or required evidence item.
Structured follow-up requirement data persists on the implementation follow-up task in tracked queue/spec/state output and is not limited to copied prose in description or acceptance text.

Each structured reviewer blocker records a stable category, the expected evidence or checks needed to satisfy it, and a status shape that can later be evaluated by implementation and review completion logic.

Implementation and review conversation references continue to be preserved on follow-up tasks or related state, but those references are not the only fields used to determine whether a blocker is satisfied.
Focused unit coverage proves review feedback is transformed into structured follow-up requirements and survives serialization and reload paths without losing blocker details.

tasks.title: Enforce blocker satisfaction before noop completion or reviewer approval
tasks.description: Update implementation follow-up completion and reviewer decision logic so unresolved structured reviewer blockers prevent `noop` completion, prevent merge or done transitions, and block reviewer approval or auto-approval unless the blockers are satisfied or explicitly dismissed by policy. Record which follow-up addressed each blocker and what new evidence was supplied so approval decisions rely on structured state instead of repeated review rounds or conversation continuity alone. Likely touch points include follow-up completion logic, reviewer gating, auto-approval paths, and queue/review state reconstruction under `src/autonomy-v2/commands/`, `src/sync/`, and any reviewer-control logic in `src/server/control-plane/` or related runtime state modules.
acceptance: An implementation follow-up that makes no code changes and records no new required evidence cannot transition to done, merged, or equivalent successful completion while one or more structured reviewer blockers remain unresolved.

Reviewer approval and any reviewer auto-approval path are blocked when unresolved structured blockers remain open, including unresolved verification blockers carried across repeated implementation/review rounds.
When policy explicitly dismisses a blocker, the decision is represented in structured state so reviewer approval can proceed only for blockers marked satisfied or dismissed by policy.

Queue/state or PR-history-facing data shows which reviewer blockers were opened, which follow-up addressed each blocker, whether the blocker is satisfied, and what evidence or check result was recorded.
Existing implementation and review conversation resume behavior remains intact after the enforcement changes.

Unit tests cover noop-blocking completion behavior and reviewer approval gating, and a smoke test covers a focused verification request flowing from review to follow-up to eventual approval once the structured blocker is satisfied.
